# svggroup.py

[简体中文](svggroup.zh.md) ｜ **English** ｜ [← Back to README](../../README.en.md)

SvgGroupElement: an SVG file imported as an editable group.

---

## Classes and methods

### `SvgGroupElement`

An imported SVG group: the whole file is parsed into a node tree inside a `<g>`, so it behaves exactly like a normal group.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `walk()` | Walk every SVG node inside this group, depth first. |
| `elements()` | Always empty: imported SVG content is bare nodes, which have no element objects. |
| `bbox()` | Bounding box of the imported content. |
| `get_x()` | Read the x this group was placed at. |
| `get_y()` | Read the y this group was placed at. |
| `get_scale()` | Read the scale factor. |
| `get_svg_file()` | Read the SVG file this group was built from. |
| `set_svg_file(value)` | Set svg_file; the same as `update(svg_file=value)`. |
| `set_x(value)` | Set x; the same as `update(x=value)`. |
| `set_y(value)` | Set y; the same as `update(y=value)`. |
| `set_scale(value)` | Set scale; the same as `update(scale=value)`. |

## Full example

Run it directly in PyCharm, or from the command line: `python malight/elements/svggroup.py`

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os

    from malight import Malight, ColorName

    _out = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__),
                                        "..", "..", "output"))
    os.makedirs(_out, exist_ok=True)

    # Build an external SVG to work with: demo only, use your own file in a project
    # attribute colours: several copies stay independent (class rules are document-global and override each other)
    badge_path = os.path.join(_out, "sample_badge.svg")
    with open(badge_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write('''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="120" height="100">
  <rect x="6" y="6" width="108" height="88" rx="14" fill="#4dabf7"/>
  <circle cx="44" cy="50" r="20" fill="#ffd43b"/>
  <text x="72" y="58" font-size="18" fill="#ffffff">SVG</text>
</svg>''')

    pen = Malight(os.path.join(_out, "demo_svggroup"), width=620, height=360)
    pen.set_background_color(ColorName.WHITESMOKE)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Import as a group: an element, used like any group
    #    recolouring goes through the tools functions
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    from malight.tools import replace_svg_node_color, svg_node_colors

    g = pen.import_svg_as_group(badge_path, x=40, y=50, scale=1.2)
    print("colours used:", svg_node_colors(g.node))
    replace_svg_node_color(g.node, "white", "#ff0000")     # a colour in an attribute
    replace_svg_node_color(g.node, "#4dabf7", "#2a9d8f")   # a colour inside a <style> block
    print("after recolouring:", svg_node_colors(g.node))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2) It is a normal group too: transforms, filters and clone all work
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    g.rotate(-8, cx=100, cy=100)
    print("bounding box:", tuple(round(v, 1) for v in g.bbox()))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) Walk the nodes: imported nodes have no element objects
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    shapes = [n.tag for n in g.walk() if n.tag in ("rect", "circle", "text")]
    print("content nodes:", shapes)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4) Import the same file twice, recolour each independently
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    g2 = pen.import_svg_as_group(badge_path, x=320, y=50, scale=1.2)
    replace_svg_node_color(g2.node, "#4dabf7", "#e76f51")
    replace_svg_node_color(g2.node, "#ffd43b", "#f4a261")
    g2.set_filter(pen.fx.shadow(4, 5, 5))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5) A partial update moves it without losing the recolouring
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    g2.update(y=200)
    print("bbox after moving:", tuple(round(v, 1) for v in g2.bbox()))

    pen.finish()
```
